replaces.change: The bundled 'healthy chicken salad' seasoned 50 g of chicken with 50 g of soy sauce plus fish sauce - 1,394 mg/serving, more sodium than a fast-food burger, from a recipe with barely any food in it. The rewrite triples the chicken to a realistic portion, poaches it gently so it stays juicy, and dresses the salad with one tablespoon of soy balanced by lime and honey - no fish sauce. Poaching also means the chicken carries the salad without heavy mayo.

ingredients.name: cucumber
ingredients.note: halved lengthwise, sliced thick on the bias

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: half a red onion, sliced paper thin

ingredients.name: jalapeño
ingredients.note: seeded if you like, sliced into fine rings

steps.text: Poach the chicken: lay the breasts in a skillet just wide enough to hold them, add water to come halfway up their sides, and bring it to the barest simmer over medium-low heat. Cover and cook gently for 10-12 minutes, flipping once.

The chicken is done when an instant-read thermometer pushed into the thickest part reads 165°F / 74°C. Lift it out and rest it on a board for 5 minutes, then shred with two forks; it should pull apart in soft curls.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: While the chicken rests, salt the cucumber slices lightly in a colander and leave them 10 minutes; pat dry. This seasons them through and keeps the salad from pooling water.

Make the dressing in the salad bowl: whisk the soy sauce, juice of 1 1/2 limes, honey, and oil until the honey dissolves. TASTE IT - it should be sour first, then salty-sweet; add the remaining lime if needed.
Toss the cucumber, red onion, and jalapeño rings through the dressing and let them sit 2 minutes.
Add the romaine, cilantro, and the warm shredded chicken and toss once more - the warmth will soften the lettuce edges slightly, which is what you want. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

nutrition_per_serving.basis: USDA FoodData Central values committed in apps/ios/Resources/usda_ingredient_catalog.sqlite (matched fdc_id per ingredient in tables/nutrition-map.json), plus the app's shipped core-ingredient table (data.json) for items without an fdc_id; scaled by evidenced gram quantities
